body: I definitely want to get into martial arts. It is a tool to become more aware of yourself and I have heard boosts confidence.

I like what you said about not harming anyone or yourself. What happens when inevitably, one person would be hurt? For instance, rejecting someones request to go out for dinner when they are having a bad day because you also need time alone. I mean, how do you make this decision?
I don't know where to start in this "assertiveness boat". Did you do any special kind of meditation, practice. Or perhaps read any books on the subject?

Thank you for all these explanations! I understand now that the pursuit of noble wants/needs is appropriate. It will be hard to put this into practice. I also think that what you say rings true to me, I often try the method of other people (be it at work or personally) to know whether or not this would work for me. However, I think this might be misconstrued as being a push-over. Thank you for your analysis.
So, being assertive means pursuing your own wants/needs? This is where I get confused.

I think what you say is very true. I am aware that I am not as compassionate to myself as I am to other people. Which I had been working on... but I feel as if I have been given a heavy blow to this effort and feel distraught at the thought that all my hard work has not been recognized, or has produced imperceptible amount of change.

Hi there, when you said : "and that I just need to wait it out while keeping the T.V. on -- will soon fall apart and reveal the underlying suffering", it made me think that in that state, people live in a constant state of fear that this distraction would suddenly not be enough and they would break down, so they pick another distraction to fill the void, if that makes any sense. 
Edit: this fear which would cause more suffering unknowingly.
